source_packets.population_and_limitations: Otherwise healthy children >=6 months; exclude recurrent disease, tubes, craniofacial abnormalities and immunocompromise.

claims.statement: AOM requires acute symptoms such as ear pain, middle-ear fluid, and inflammatory otoscopic findings; effusion alone does not establish AOM.
Mild AOM in otherwise healthy children at least six months old permits observation with analgesia and assured reassessment within 24–48 hours; worsening requires reassessment/treatment.
Bulging tympanic membrane supports AOM; reduced pneumatic mobility supports middle-ear effusion.

source_packets.population_and_limitations: Known or suspected pediatric asthma; assess alternative diagnoses. Adjunctive escalation does not replace initial resuscitation.

claims.statement: Chest radiography can investigate persistent asymmetry or suspected complications; typical exacerbations do not require routine radiography.
claims.source_locator: Assessment of respiratory distress, ancillary tests

claims.statement: Consider intravenous magnesium after incomplete response to conventional therapy over 1–2 hours, with cardiorespiratory monitoring and specialist consultation.
Initial treatment includes inhaled bronchodilators, systemic steroids for moderate/severe exacerbations, and oxygen for hypoxemia.
Reduced air entry and wheezing are assessment findings in an asthma exacerbation.

source_packets.population_and_limitations: Adult upper-tract stones. No pregnancy, pediatric, dose-specific or definitive-procedure comparison claims.

claims.statement: Infected ureteral obstruction requires resuscitation, intravenous antibiotics and prompt drainage; definitive stone treatment waits for infection control.
NSAID-containing opioid-sparing analgesia is effective for renal colic; minimize opioid exposure.
Symptom resolution or reported stone passage does not reliably exclude obstruction; follow-up imaging should confirm passage.
Fever, leukocytosis and an obstructing ureteral stone describe the trial population comparing drainage routes.
Stone prevention preserves dietary calcium, preferably from food; the recommended intake is 1000–1200 mg/day, with any needed supplements taken with meals.
Dietary counselling is warranted even after an initial stone episode; stone composition informs prevention.
claims.source_locator: General dietary measures; Importance of stone analysis

source_packets.population_and_limitations: Adult AUD; medication decisions require explicit contraindication assessment. Exclude pregnancy and complex concurrent substance-use treatment decisions.

claims.statement: A high-risk positive alcohol screen requires a DSM-5-TR diagnostic interview.

Previous withdrawal seizures and PAWSS inform risk; high-risk withdrawal warrants short-term benzodiazepines, ideally inpatient. Closely monitored outpatient care is an alternative when inpatient barriers exist.
For adult moderate/severe AUD, naltrexone supports reduction or abstinence; acamprosate supports abstinence.
Current opioid use, acute hepatitis or liver failure contraindicate naltrexone; severe renal impairment contraindicates acamprosate.

source_packets.population_and_limitations: Children with typical croup; assess red flags and atypical age/course. No dose calculations are authorized by this packet.

claims.statement: Typical croup combines barking cough, hoarseness and inspiratory stridor.
Corticosteroids benefit mild through severe croup; oral dexamethasone is preferred when tolerated.
Nebulized epinephrine is recommended for moderate/severe croup; benefit wanes after two hours.
After dexamethasone and nebulized epinephrine, discharge is supported when symptoms do not recur during 2–4 hours of observation.
Audible resting stridor and visible resting chest indrawing characterize moderate croup.
Toxic appearance, drooling and dysphagia suggest an alternative serious cause of stridor.

source_packets.discipline_routing_note: SURG is the frozen allocation discipline for SU-OT-52; source and patient population are pediatric.

proposed_decisions.statement: Diagnose AOM using acute symptoms and inflammatory otoscopy.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: AOM versus effusion or external-ear disease; no prior AOM target found.

proposed_decisions.statement: Select observation with analgesia and reassessment for mild eligible AOM.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Antibiotic timing in an ear infection; prior PED targets concerned bronchiolitis.

proposed_decisions.statement: Investigate persistent asymmetric findings during an asthma exacerbation with chest radiography.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Asthma appears historically as a bronchiolitis diagnostic competitor, not this complication-directed investigation decision.

proposed_decisions.statement: Select monitored intravenous magnesium for incomplete response to initial asthma therapy.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Adjunct escalation after asthma therapy differs from prior bronchiolitis diagnosis/support decisions.

proposed_decisions.statement: Follow high-risk alcohol screening with a diagnostic interview.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Screening-to-diagnosis transition differs from previous depression diagnosis/severity/suicide targets.

proposed_decisions.statement: Choose inpatient short-term benzodiazepine withdrawal care after previous withdrawal seizures.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Withdrawal complication prevention differs from depression suicide-risk disposition.

proposed_decisions.statement: Select naltrexone for an eligible adult seeking reduced drinking.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Treatment-goal medication matching differs from prior depression treatment thresholds.

proposed_decisions.statement: Select acamprosate for abstinence when ongoing prescribed opioids preclude naltrexone.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Contraindication-based selection differs from reduction-goal selection; independent redundancy review must confirm material distinctness.

proposed_decisions.statement: Recognize croup from its upper-airway presentation.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Upper-airway diagnosis differs from previously optimized bronchiolitis targets.

proposed_decisions.statement: Select oral dexamethasone even for mild croup.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Tests anti-inflammatory treatment of mild croup rather than bronchiolitis support.

proposed_decisions.statement: Add nebulized epinephrine for moderate croup with resting stridor.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Urgent upper-airway rescue differs from mild-croup anti-inflammatory therapy; independent distinctness review remains necessary.

proposed_decisions.statement: Determine discharge readiness after sustained post-treatment observation.
proposed_decisions.educational_distinctness: Disposition depends on transient rescue-drug effect, not initial croup severity alone.

reuse_audit.method: Deterministic recursive JSON object scan by study_unit_id/allocation_address_id, plus text search of all QGEN artifacts and source populations
reuse_audit.historical_overlap: SU-P-146 occurs as a diagnostic competitor for bronchiolitis; proposed asthma decisions use new learner relationships.

existing_related_claims.relevance: Existing initial stone imaging and conservative-management claims found; neither establishes the selected acute analgesia/follow-up/dietary decisions. Renal candidates subsequently excluded for unclear canonical scope.

obstacles: Independent source entailment, clinical fact, scope, educational distinctness and feature-identity review are pending.
These bounded claims do not establish whole-address completeness or contrast readiness.
Acamprosate decision requires explicit renal eligibility and naltrexone decision requires explicit opioid/liver contraindication assessment.
Initial renal-colic imaging selection was excluded pending reconciliation with newer CAR genitourinary imaging guidance.
Asthma incomplete-response feature needs an operational definition in relation predicates; it must not become an ungrounded severity label.
Renal-stone author candidates excluded before independent review because their canonical MCC mapping is weak and narrowly restricted; do not count them in the fresh universe.
Croup is canonically routed SURG but adds a pediatric clinical population; final pilot discipline counts must follow frozen routing and disclose this population skew.
All sources were read through current publisher/Canadian authority URLs; this is author research, not independent clinical or source verification.
